sanskrit: sarvathā yuddham evāham āśaṃsāmi paraiḥ saha nimittāni hi sarvāṇi tathā prādurbhavanti me
english: In every way I foresee war with our enemies; for all the omens appear to me as portending just that.

sanskrit: mṛgāḥ śakuntāś ca vadanti ghoraṃ; hastyaśvamukhyeṣu niśāmukheṣu ghorāṇi rūpāṇi tathaiva cāgnir; varṇān bahūn puṣyati ghorarūpān manuṣyalokakṣapaṇo 'tha ghoro; no ced anuprāpta ihāntakaḥ syāt
english: Beasts and birds cry out in dreadful tones; at dusk, terrible forms appear among the foremost elephants and horses; fire blazes forth in many ghastly hues — destruction-bearing and fearsome. Were the destroyer not already at hand, it would not be so.

sanskrit: śastrāṇi patraṃ kavacān rathāṃś ca; nāgān dhvajāṃś ca pratipādayitvā yodhāś ca sarve kṛtaniśramās te; bhavantu hastyaśvaratheṣu yattāḥ sāṃgrāmikaṃ te yad upārjanīyaṃ; sarvaṃ samagraṃ kuru tan narendra
english: Having arrayed weapons, armour, chariots, and elephants, and all banners, and with every warrior rested and ready — let them be alert upon elephants, horses, and chariots. Whatever must be won in battle, make all of it complete, O lord of men.

sanskrit: duryodhano na hy alam adya dātuṃ; jīvaṃs tavaitan nṛpate kathaṃ cit yat te purastād abhavat samṛddhaṃ; dyūte hṛtaṃ pāṇḍavamukhya rājyam
english: Duryodhana is utterly unable to restore it to you while he yet lives, O king — that prosperous realm that was once yours, O foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, stolen from you at the dice game.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca yathā yathaiva śāntiḥ syāt kurūṇāṃ madhusūdana tathā tathaiva bhāṣethā mā sma yuddhena bhīṣayeḥ
english: Bhīmasena said: Speak only in whatever way peace may come about for the Kurus, O Madhusūdana; do not threaten them with war.

sanskrit: amarṣī nityasaṃrabdhaḥ śreyodveṣī mahāmanāḥ nograṃ duryodhano vācyaḥ sāmnaivainaṃ samācareḥ
english: Intolerant, perpetually enraged, contemptuous of what is good — though high-minded — Duryodhana must not be addressed harshly; deal with him through conciliation alone.

sanskrit: prakṛtyā pāpasattvaś ca tulyacetāś ca dasyubhiḥ aiśvaryamadamattaś ca kṛtavairaś ca pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: He is wicked by nature, of the same mind as brigands, intoxicated with the pride of sovereignty, and one who has made enmity with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: adīrghadarśī niṣṭhūrī kṣeptā krūraparākramaḥ dīrghamanyur aneyaś ca pāpātmā nikṛtipriyaḥ
english: Shortsighted, cruel, contemptuous, ferocious in his valour, long-bearing in anger, ungovernable, evil-souled, and fond of deceit —

sanskrit: mriyetāpi na bhajyeta naiva jahyāt svakaṃ matam tādṛśena śamaṃ kṛṣṇa manye paramaduṣkaram
english: Even if he were to die, he would not relent, nor would he ever abandon his own view. Peace with such a one, O Kṛṣṇa, I consider supremely difficult.

sanskrit: suhṛdām apy avācīnas tyaktadharmaḥ priyānṛtaḥ pratihanty eva suhṛdāṃ vācaś caiva manāṃsi ca
english: He is ungrateful even toward friends, has abandoned righteousness, is fond of falsehood, and strikes back against the words and minds of his own well-wishers.

sanskrit: sa manyuvaśam āpannaḥ svabhāvaṃ duṣṭam āsthitaḥ svabhāvāt pāpam anveti tṛṇais tunna ivoragaḥ
english: Fallen under the sway of anger and fixed in his corrupt nature, he pursues evil according to his very character — like a serpent pricked by blades of grass.

sanskrit: duryodhano hi yat senaḥ sarvathā viditas tava yacchīlo yatsvabhāvaś ca yadbalo yatparākramaḥ
english: Duryodhana along with his army is known to you in every way — what his disposition is, what his nature, what his strength, and what his prowess.

sanskrit: purā prasannāḥ kuravaḥ sahaputrās tathā vayam indrajyeṣṭhā ivābhūma modamānāḥ sabāndhavāḥ
english: In former days the Kurus with their sons, and we as well, lived joyfully together with our kinsmen, as though with Indra foremost among us.

sanskrit: duryodhanasya krodhena bhāratā madhusūdana dhakṣyante śiśirāpāye vanānīva hutāśanaiḥ
english: Through Duryodhana's wrath, O Madhusūdana, the Bharatas will be consumed like forests by fire at the close of winter.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśeme rājānaḥ prakhyātā madhusūdana ye samuccicchidur jñātīn suhṛdaś ca sabāndhavān
english: These eighteen renowned kings, O Madhusūdana, utterly destroyed their kinsmen, friends, and relatives alike —

sanskrit: asurāṇāṃ samṛddhānāṃ jvalatām iva tejasā paryāyakāle dharmasya prāpte balir ajāyata
english: Among the flourishing Asuras blazing with splendour, when the appointed time of righteousness arrived, Bali was born —

sanskrit: haihayānām udāvarto nīpānāṃ janamejayaḥ bahulas tālajaṅghānāṃ kṛmīṇām uddhato vasuḥ
english: Udavarta among the Haihayas, Janamejaya among the Nipas, Bahula among the Tālajaṅghas, Uddhata Vasu among the Krimis —

sanskrit: ajabinduḥ suvīrāṇāṃ surāṣṭrāṇāṃ kuśarddhikaḥ arkajaś ca balīhānāṃ cīnānāṃ dhautamūlakaḥ
english: Ajabindu among the Suviras, Kusardhika among the Saurashtras, Arkaja among the Balihas, Dhautamulaka among the Chinas —

sanskrit: hayagrīvo videhānāṃ varapraś ca mahaujasām bāhuḥ sundaravegānāṃ dīptākṣāṇāṃ purūravāḥ
english: Hayagrīva among the Videhas, Varapra among the mighty Mahaujasas, Bahu among the Sundaravegas, Pururava among the Diptakshas —

sanskrit: sahajaś cedimatsyānāṃ pracetānāṃ bṛhadbalaḥ dhāraṇaś cendravatsānāṃ mukuṭānāṃ vigāhanaḥ
english: Sahaja among the Cedi-Matsyas, Bṛhadbala among the Pracetas, Dhāraṇa among the Indravatsas, Vigahana among the Mukutas —

sanskrit: śamaś ca nandivegānām ity ete kulapāṃsanāḥ yugānte kṛṣṇa saṃbhūtāḥ kuleṣu puruṣādhamāḥ
english: And Shama among the Nandivegas — these disgracers of their families, O Kṛṣṇa, were born at the end of their respective ages as the lowest of men within their clans.

sanskrit: apy ayaṃ naḥ kurūṇāṃ syād yugānte kālasaṃbhṛtaḥ duryodhanaḥ kulāṅgāro jaghanyaḥ pāpapūruṣaḥ
english: Could this Duryodhana be for us Kurus that brand upon the family, nurtured by time at the end of the age — the lowest of men, a sinful wretch?

sanskrit: tasmān mṛdu śanair enaṃ brūyā dharmārthasaṃhitam kāmānubandhabahulaṃ nogram ugraparākramam
english: Therefore speak to him gently and gradually, with words rooted in righteousness and benefit, richly invoking his desires — not harshly, for he is ferocious in valour.

sanskrit: api duryodhanaṃ kṛṣṇa sarve vayam adhaścarāḥ nīcair bhūtvānuyāsyāmo mā sma no bharatā naśan
english: O Kṛṣṇa, let all of us even bow low before Duryodhana; let us descend to humility and follow along — only let the Bharatas not perish.

sanskrit: apy udāsīnavṛttiḥ syād yathā naḥ kurubhiḥ saha vāsudeva tathā kāryaṃ na kurūn anayaḥ spṛśet
english: If only there could be a neutral standing — O Vāsudeva, act in whatever way allows us to live alongside the Kurus without dishonour touching them.

sanskrit: vācyaḥ pitāmaho vṛddho ye ca kṛṣṇa sabhāsadaḥ bhrātṝṇām astu saubhrātraṃ dhārtarāṣṭraḥ praśāmyatām
english: Speak also to the aged grandfather Bhīṣma and to the members of the assembly, O Kṛṣṇa: let there be brotherhood among the brothers, and let the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra be appeased.

sanskrit: aham etad bravīmy evaṃ rājā caiva praśaṃsati arjuno naiva yuddhārthī bhūyasī hi dayārjune
english: I say this, and the king agrees; Arjuna likewise is no seeker of war — for compassion runs deep in Arjuna.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā mahābāhuḥ keśavaḥ prahasann iva abhūtapūrvaṃ bhīmasya mārdavopagataṃ vacaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing these unprecedented words of Bhīma, who had fallen into such uncharacteristic softness, the mighty-armed Keśava smiled.

sanskrit: girer iva laghutvaṃ tac chītatvam iva pāvake matvā rāmānujaḥ śauriḥ śārṅgadhanvā vṛkodaram
english: Reckoning it like lightness in a mountain, or coolness in fire, the younger brother of Rāma — Śauri, bearer of the Śārṅga bow — addressed Vṛkodara:

sanskrit: saṃtejayaṃs tadā vāgbhir mātariśveva pāvakam uvāca bhīmam āsīnaṃ kṛpayābhipariplutam
english: Enkindling him with words as the wind kindles fire, Kṛṣṇa spoke to Bhīma who sat there overwhelmed with pity.

sanskrit: tvam anyadā bhīmasena yuddham eva praśaṃsasi vadhābhinandinaḥ krūrān dhārtarāṣṭrān mimardiṣuḥ
english: At other times, O Bhīmasena, you praise only war, eager to slay and crush those cruel sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: na ca svapiṣi jāgarṣi nyubjaḥ śeṣe paraṃtapa ghorām aśāntāṃ ruśatīṃ sadā vācaṃ prabhāṣase
english: You do not sleep but lie awake face-down, O scorcher of foes, ever speaking harsh, disturbing, and wrathful words.

sanskrit: niḥśvasann agnivarṇena saṃtaptaḥ svena manyunā apraśāntamanā bhīma sadhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: Breathing out breath the colour of fire, consumed by your own rage, with your mind unquenched, O Bhīma — like a fire still trailing smoke.

sanskrit: ekānte niṣṭanañ śeṣe bhārārta iva durbalaḥ api tvāṃ ke cid unmantaṃ manyante 'tadvido janāḥ
english: You lie alone in corners groaning, like one weighed down and weary; some who do not know you even think you have lost your mind.

sanskrit: ārujya vṛkṣān nirmūlān gajaḥ paribhujann iva nighnan padbhiḥ kṣitiṃ bhīma niṣṭanan paridhāvasi
english: Wrenching up trees and uprooting them like an elephant snapping branches, striking the ground with your feet, O Bhīma, you roam about groaning.

sanskrit: nāsmiñ jane 'bhiramase rahaḥ kṣiyasi pāṇḍava nānyaṃ niśi divā vāpi kadā cid abhinandasi
english: You take no pleasure in the company of people, O Pāṇḍava, but dwell in solitude; neither night nor day do you ever greet anyone with joy.

sanskrit: akasmāt smayamānaś ca rahasy āsse rudann iva jānvor mūrdhānam ādhāya ciram āsse pramīlitaḥ
english: Suddenly you smile for no reason in private, then sit as though weeping; you sit for long with your head resting on your knees, eyes half-closed.

sanskrit: bhrukuṭiṃ ca punaḥ kurvann oṣṭhau ca vilihann iva abhīkṣṇaṃ dṛśyase bhīma sarvaṃ tan manyukāritam
english: Again and again you are seen knitting your brows and licking your lips — all of it, O Bhīma, is the work of rage.

sanskrit: yathā purastāt savitā dṛśyate śukram uccaran yathā ca paścān nirmukto dhruvaṃ paryeti raśmivān
english: Just as the sun is seen rising brilliant in the east and, once released, revolves with its rays steadfastly in the west —

sanskrit: tathā satyaṃ bravīmy etan nāsti tasya vyatikramaḥ hantāhaṃ gadayābhyetya duryodhanam amarṣaṇam
english: So truly I say: there is no deviation from it — 'I will approach the intolerant Duryodhana with my mace and slay him!' —

sanskrit: iti sma madhye bhrātṝṇāṃ satyenālabhase gadām tasya te praśame buddhir dhīyate 'dya paraṃtapa
english: Thus you once solemnly grasped your mace in the midst of your brothers, pledging it. Yet now, O scorcher of foes, your mind turns toward peace with him.

sanskrit: aho yuddhapratīpāni yuddhakāla upasthite paśyasīvāpratīpāni kiṃ tvāṃ bhīr bhīma vindati
english: Ah — when the time of battle is upon us, you see as contrary to war what is not contrary to it at all. Has fear overtaken you, O Bhīma?

sanskrit: aho pārtha nimittāni viparītāni paśyasi svapnānte jāgarānte ca tasmāt praśamam icchasi
english: Ah, O Pārtha, you see omens as reversed — both in the borderland of sleep and in full waking — and therefore you desire peace.

sanskrit: aho nāśaṃsase kiṃ cit puṃstvaṃ klība ivātmani kaśmalenābhipanno 'si tena te vikṛtaṃ manaḥ
english: Ah — you hope for nothing of your own manliness, like a eunuch! You are seized by faint-heartedness, and by that your mind is perverted.

sanskrit: udvepate te hṛdayaṃ manas te praviṣīdati ūrustambhagṛhīto 'si tasmāt praśamam icchasi
english: Your heart trembles, your mind sinks into despondency, you are gripped by the paralysis of your thighs — and therefore you desire peace.

sanskrit: anityaṃ kila martyasya cittaṃ pārtha calācalam vātavegapracalitā aṣṭhīlā śālmaler iva
english: The mind of a mortal is indeed impermanent, O Pārtha, ever wavering — like the seed pod of a silk-cotton tree shaken loose by a gust of wind.

sanskrit: tavaiṣā vikṛtā buddhir gavāṃ vāg iva mānuṣī manāṃsi pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ majjayaty aplavān iva
english: This corrupted understanding of yours — like the speech of cattle become human — is drowning the minds of the sons of Pāṇḍu like men who cannot swim.

sanskrit: idaṃ me mahad āścaryaṃ parvatasyeva sarpaṇam yadīdṛśaṃ prabhāṣethā bhīmasenāsamaṃ vacaḥ
english: This is a great wonder to me — like a mountain moving — that you, Bhīmasena, should speak words so unlike yourself.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā svāni karmāṇi kule janma ca bhārata uttiṣṭhasva viṣādaṃ mā kṛthā vīra sthiro bhava
english: Seeing your own deeds and your birth in this lineage, O Bhārata, rise up! Do not give way to despondency, O hero — be steadfast.

sanskrit: na caitad anurūpaṃ te yat te glānir ariṃdama yad ojasā na labhate kṣatriyo na tad aśnute
english: This faint-heartedness is not fitting for you, O crusher of foes. What a warrior cannot win through prowess, he cannot enjoy either.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathokto vāsudevena nityamanyur amarṣaṇaḥ sadaśvavat samādhāvad babhāṣe tadanantaram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, the ever-wrathful and intolerant one sprang forward like a fine horse and then spoke in reply.

sanskrit: anyathā māṃ cikīrṣantam anyathā manyase 'cyuta praṇītabhāvam atyantaṃ yudhi satyaparākramam
english: You think of me as different from what I intend, O Acyuta — one who is utterly disciplined in spirit and of proven valour in battle.

sanskrit: vettha dāśārha sattvaṃ me dīrghakālaṃ sahoṣitaḥ uta vā māṃ na jānāsi plavan hrada ivālpavaḥ tasmād apratirūpābhir vāgbhir māṃ tvaṃ samarchasi
english: You know my character, O descendant of Dāśārha, having lived with me a long time — or do you perhaps not know me, like shallow water mistaking itself for a deep lake? Therefore you address me with words that do not suit me.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi bhīmasenaṃ māṃ jānan kaś cana mādhava brūyād apratirūpāṇi yathā māṃ vaktum arhasi
english: How could anyone who knows me as Bhīmasena, O Mādhava, speak to me in such unsuitable terms — just as you have seen fit to speak to me?

sanskrit: tasmād idaṃ pravakṣyāmi vacanaṃ vṛṣṇinandana ātmanaḥ pauruṣaṃ caiva balaṃ ca na samaṃ paraiḥ
english: Therefore I shall declare this, O joy of the Vṛṣṇis — my own manliness and strength, which are not equal to those of my enemies but surpass them.

sanskrit: sarvathā nāryakarmaitat praśaṃsā svayam ātmanaḥ ativādāpaviddhas tu vakṣyāmi balam ātmanaḥ
english: Self-praise is in no way a noble act; yet pierced by those sharp words, I shall speak of my own strength.

sanskrit: paśyeme rodasī kṛṣṇa yayor āsann imāḥ prajāḥ acale cāpy anante ca pratiṣṭhe sarvamātarau
english: Look upon these two — heaven and earth, O Kṛṣṇa — within whom all these creatures dwell, both immovable and infinite, established as the mothers of all.

sanskrit: yadīme sahasā kruddhe sameyātāṃ śile iva aham ete nigṛhṇīyāṃ bāhubhyāṃ sacarācare
english: If these two, suddenly enraged, were to rush together like two slabs of rock, I could hold them apart with my two arms — along with all the moving and unmoving creation between them.

sanskrit: paśyaitad antaraṃ bāhvor mahāparighayor iva ya etat prāpya mucyeta na taṃ paśyāmi pūruṣam
english: Look at the span between these arms of mine, like two great iron bolts — I see no man who, once caught within it, could escape.

sanskrit: himavāṃś ca samudraś ca vajrī ca balabhit svayam mayābhipannaṃ trāyeran balam āsthāya na trayaḥ
english: Even the Himālayas, the ocean, and Indra the thunderbolt-wielder himself — if I were to attack, those three could not rescue anyone by relying on their strength.

sanskrit: yudhyeyaṃ kṣatriyān sarvān pāṇḍaveṣv ātatāyinaḥ adhaḥ pādatalenaitān adhiṣṭhāsyāmi bhūtale
english: I could fight all the warriors who have set upon the Pāṇḍavas and crush them underfoot upon the ground.

sanskrit: na hi tvaṃ nābhijānāsi mama vikramam acyuta yathā mayā vinirjitya rājāno vaśagāḥ kṛtāḥ
english: Surely you do not fail to know my prowess, O Acyuta — how I subdued kings and brought them under our sway.

sanskrit: atha cen māṃ na jānāsi sūryasyevodyataḥ prabhām vigāḍhe yudhi saṃbādhe vetsyase māṃ janārdana
english: But if you do not know me — as men do not know the risen sun's brilliance — you shall come to know me, O Janārdana, in the thick and press of battle.

sanskrit: kiṃ mātyavākṣīḥ paruṣair vraṇaṃ sūcyā ivānagha yathāmati bravīmy etad viddhi mām adhikaṃ tataḥ
english: Why did you pierce me with those harsh words, like a needle into a wound, O sinless one? I speak as best I can — know that I am greater still than what I say.

sanskrit: draṣṭāsi yudhi saṃbādhe pravṛtte vaiśase 'hani mayā praṇunnān mātaṅgān rathinaḥ sādinas tathā
english: You shall see it on the day of carnage, when battle is joined in fierce press — elephants driven before me, and likewise charioteers and cavalry.

sanskrit: tathā narān abhikruddhaṃ nighnantaṃ kṣatriyarṣabhān draṣṭā māṃ tvaṃ ca lokaś ca vikarṣantaṃ varān varān
english: You and the world shall behold me furiously slaying men and foremost warriors, dragging away the best of them one after another.

sanskrit: na me sīdanti majjāno na mamodvepate manaḥ sarvalokād abhikruddhān na bhayaṃ vidyate mama
english: My marrow does not melt, my mind does not tremble; I feel no fear even when all the world turns against me in rage.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu sauhṛdam evaitat kṛpayā madhusūdana sarvāṃs titikṣe saṃkleśān mā sma no bharatā naśan
english: But it is only this friendship, O Madhusūdana — compassion — that makes me endure all these hardships: let not the Bharatas perish.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca bhāvaṃ jijñāsamāno 'haṃ praṇayād idam abruvam na cākṣepān na pāṇḍityān na krodhān na vivakṣayā
english: The Blessed Lord said: It was out of affection, wishing to test your spirit, that I spoke thus — not out of insult, not out of pedantry, not out of anger, and not out of a desire to argue.

sanskrit: vedāhaṃ tava māhātmyam uta te veda yad balam uta te veda karmāṇi na tvāṃ paribhavāmy aham
english: I know your greatness; I know the strength that is yours; I know your deeds. I do not disparage you.

sanskrit: yathā cātmani kalyāṇaṃ saṃbhāvayasi pāṇḍava sahasraguṇam apy etat tvayi saṃbhāvayāmy aham
english: Whatever good qualities you perceive in yourself, O Pāṇḍava, I reckon them in you thousandfold.

sanskrit: yādṛśe ca kule janma sarvarājābhipūjite bandhubhiś ca suhṛdbhiś ca bhīma tvam asi tādṛśaḥ
english: And in such a lineage — honoured by all kings, by kinsmen and by friends — O Bhīma, you are exactly as that birth demands.

sanskrit: jijñāsanto hi dharmasya saṃdigdhasya vṛkodara paryāyaṃ na vyavasyanti daivamānuṣayor janāḥ
english: For men who seek to understand the turn of doubtful dharma, O Vṛkodara, cannot resolve the alternation of the divine and the human.

sanskrit: sa eva hetur bhūtvā hi puruṣasyārthasiddhiṣu vināśe 'pi sa evāsya saṃdigdhaṃ karma pauruṣam
english: That very same cause which becomes the means of a person's success becomes the cause of his ruin as well — and thus human effort remains uncertain.

sanskrit: anyathā paridṛṣṭāni kavibhir doṣadarśibhiḥ anyathā parivartante vegā iva nabhasvataḥ
english: What is seen one way by discerning poets who perceive flaws turns out another way — like the gusts of the wind veering unpredictably.

sanskrit: sumantritaṃ sunītaṃ ca nyāyataś copapāditam kṛtaṃ mānuṣyakaṃ karma daivenāpi virudhyate
english: Even what is well-counselled, well-ordered, properly supported, and rightly done by human effort is opposed by fate.

sanskrit: daivam apy akṛtaṃ karma pauruṣeṇa vihanyate śītam uṣṇaṃ tathā varṣaṃ kṣutpipāse ca bhārata
english: Divine fate too, if unassisted by action, is foiled by human exertion — just as cold, heat, rain, hunger, and thirst are overcome, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yad anyad diṣṭabhāvasya puruṣasya svayaṃkṛtam tasmād anavarodhaś ca vidyate tatra lakṣaṇam
english: Whatever a person who is disposed to his appointed fate accomplishes through his own doing — beyond that there is no obstruction; that is the mark of it.

sanskrit: lokasya nānyato vṛttiḥ pāṇḍavānyatra karmaṇaḥ evaṃbuddhiḥ pravarteta phalaṃ syād ubhayānvayāt
english: The sustenance of the world rests on nothing else than action, O Pāṇḍava. One who understands this should act accordingly — the fruit would follow from the confluence of both.

sanskrit: ya evaṃ kṛtabuddhiḥ san karmasv eva pravartate nāsiddhau vyathate tasya na siddhau harṣam aśnute
english: He who, with this understanding firmly established, engages in action alone — neither grieves in failure nor is elated in success.
